items.question: What is the purpose of the reparameterization trick in Variational Autoencoders?
items.ground_truth_answer: The reparameterization trick z = mu(x) + sigma(x) * epsilon allows backpropagation of gradients with respect to the encoder parameters phi through the stochastic latent variable.
items.evidence_passage: The reparameterization trick z = mu(x) + sigma(x) * epsilon, where epsilon ~ N(0, I), allows backpropagation of gradients with respect to encoder parameters phi.

items.module_title: Uncertainty Quantification, Calibration, and RAG Grounding
items.section: 8.1 Model Calibration and Expected Calibration Error (ECE)
items.question: How does temperature scaling improve probability calibration while preserving classification accuracy?
items.ground_truth_answer: Temperature scaling scales logits by a learned positive scalar T without changing the argmax ranking, which keeps classification predictions intact while adjusting softmax entropy to minimize validation negative log-likelihood.
items.evidence_passage: Temperature scaling post-processes logits z via a learned scalar T > 0: p_hat = softmax(z / T). Temperature scaling preserves model accuracy (argmax remains invariant) while minimizing negative log-likelihood on validation data to achieve calibrated probabilities.

items.section: 4.2 Positional Encodings: Absolute, Relative, and RoPE
items.question: How does Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) represent relative sequence displacement?
items.ground_truth_answer: RoPE rotates key and query vectors in complex 2D planes such that the inner product depends strictly on relative displacement (m - n).
items.evidence_passage: Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE, Su et al., 2021) rotate key and query vectors in complex 2D planes: R_{Theta, m}^d x_m, ensuring that the inner product (R_m q)^T (R_n k) depends strictly on relative displacement (m - n).

items.question: Why is the dot product scaled by 1 / sqrt(d_k) in Scaled Dot-Product Attention?
items.ground_truth_answer: The scaling factor 1 / sqrt(d_k) counteracts the growth of dot products for large dimensions, which would otherwise push the softmax into regions with vanishingly small gradients.
items.evidence_passage: The scaling factor 1 / sqrt(d_k) counteracts the growth of dot products for large dimensions, which would otherwise push softmax into regions with vanishingly small gradients.

items.question: What is the role of the cross-encoder NLI verifier in an evidence-grounded AI tutor?
items.ground_truth_answer: The cross-encoder NLI verifier computes an Evidence Agreement Score between answer propositions and retrieved context, triggering calibrated abstention when evidence agreement is inadequate.
items.evidence_passage: An evidence-grounded AI tutor requires cross-encoder natural language inference (NLI) to compute an Evidence Agreement Score (EAS) between answer propositions and retrieved context, abstaining whenever max EAS falls below the calibrated conformal threshold tau.
